Local governor Veniamin Kondratyev stated that falling drone debris injured at least 40 others, and accused Kyiv of attacking civilian targets far away from military installations. It is unclear if the drone was intercepted before it landed on the beach. Ukraine has not yet commented on the strike. Sergey Aksyonov, the Moscow-installed governor of Crimea, said in a Telegram post that four people were killed in a Ukrainian strike on the Russia-annexed region. Russian military officials said they have intercepted a further 131 Ukrainian drones overnight. Kyiv did not confirm the strikes, but analysts said it was in line with the size of a recent spate of Ukrainian counter-attacks to Russian aggression. At the same time, Ukraine said that an attack on a gas station in the Dnipropetrovsk had killed three people, in keeping with a recent pattern of Russian attacks on fuel depots. Zelenskyy said Umerov would remain in charge of peace talks after being moved from his previous job as head of the Security Council advisory body. Photograph: Nikolay Doychinov/AFP/Getty Images Weather tracker Europe Analysis Weather tracker: Europe breaks more heat records as temperatures soar Magdalena Shopova for MetDesk Drought and wildfires intensify across continent, while tropical storms bring heavy rain and disruption to east Asia Europe live – latest updates Mon 10 Aug 2026 05.32 EDT Last modified on Mon 10 Aug 2026 05.43 EDT Share High pressure has dominated central and eastern Europe in early August, breaking temperature records across the region. Austria recorded a high of 41.2C (106.2F), while Slovakia reached 42.2C. Hungary hit a peak of 41.8C, surpassing a record set in 1905, while overnight temperatures remained above 28C in some areas, marking it as a tropical night. The extreme temperatures have been driven by a heat dome beneath the high-pressure system, which traps warm air close to the surface. The prolonged heat has dried out soil and vegetation, creating conditions conducive to the spread of wildfires. Fires have burned across Italy, France, Serbia and Bulgaria, damaging forests and forcing residents to evacuate. Water levels in the Danube, which flows through much of the affected region, have fallen to an all-time low . The receding river has exposed archaeological remains and wartime wreckage , including woolly mammoth bones, second world war ships and remains associated with the Roman-era Constantine’s Bridge. Low water levels have also affected energy production, reducing the efficiency of nuclear power plants in Slovakia and Serbia and forcing Hungary to shut down a plant because there was insufficient water for cooling. Meanwhile, a buoy in the Mediterranean recorded a sea-surface temperature of 33C. If verified, it would be the highest recorded in the region. In eastern Asia, Typhoon Dolphin made landfall in China on Sunday. The national observatory had issued a red alert for the storm – the highest level – for prolonged heavy rainfall , high wind speeds and extensive damage. Dolphin has since weakened to a tropical storm. Japan is braced for Typhoon Chan-hom, just days after Dolphin swept through northern Okinawa and the Amami islands. Chan-hom is expected to make landfall near the coast of Tohoku between Tuesday and Wednesday, with up to 80mph (129km/h) gusts and an atmospheric pressure of 985 hPa. A third system, Peilou, formed on Sunday in the western Pacific. Although it is not expected to make landfall in the Philippines , it is likely to strengthen the south-west monsoon, bringing further rain across the country. Other typhoons this year have intensified the monsoon, which has killed six people and displaced more than 380,000. Photograph: Kylie Cooper/Reuters Donald Trump White House launches personal attack on CNN reporter over question to Trump CNN says attack ‘beneath the office’ after Kristen Holmes asked president about Jon Ossoff’s comments on key aide Sam Levin Mon 17 Aug 2026 22.04 EDT Last modified on Mon 17 Aug 2026 22.08 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The White House launched a personal attack against a CNN reporter on Monday with a social media post that mentioned her children and accused her of asking a “disgusting and inhumane question”. A White House post targeted Kristen Holmes, a senior White House correspondent for the network, after she asked Donald Trump to respond to a widely shared comment by Democratic senator Jon Ossoff in a speech on Sunday . The Georgia senator told a crowd that Trump “doesn’t want to do the job” and instead “wants to build his ballroom and travel with Natalie on their apparently defenseless flying palace gifted by the emir of Qatar”. The comment was an apparent reference to Natalie Harp, the president’s executive assistant, fueling scrutiny of her perceived closeness to Trump. When Holmes asked Trump in the Oval Office to respond to Ossoff’s remark, the president dismissed her, calling the senator a “Pee-wee Herman lookalike”. The White House’s “rapid response” social media account posted a clip of the exchange and tagged Holmes, calling her a “disgraceful, humiliating embarrassment to her alleged profession”. The post went on to criticize her for taking a “cheap shot” at a staffer, adding: “These scumbags are the lowest of the low.” The White House later sent out another post criticizing Holmes, writing: “Someday, your children will come across your disgusting and inhumane question. They will be sickened and embarrassed to have a parent be so callous and vindictive. It’s quite troubling.” Trump also directly criticized Holmes during the Oval Office event, at one point telling her: “Quiet, quiet, quiet. You’re very disrespectful.” After she told him she worked for CNN, he responded : “Fake news, you’re fake news, you’re a loud boisterous person. You’re fake news. Be quiet. Be quiet. You’re a fake reporter and you report fake news.” He talked over her as she tried to ask a question. CNN defended Holmes in a statement , calling her “one of the most respected and accomplished journalists covering the White House”. 1:19 Trump tells CNN reporter to 'be quiet' during Oval Office clash – video The network said she had asked Trump a “tough, relevant, and newsworthy question on behalf of the American people”, writing: “Public officials are free to challenge reporting they disagree with, but personal attacks on journalists for asking questions are beneath the office and inconsistent with the principles of a free press.” Earlier, the White House director of communications also posted a series of insults targeting Ossoff in response to the senator’s speech, writing: “Jon Jackoff has to be the biggest cuck loser in politics.” Trump has a long history of aggressively attacking and insulting women in the press corps who ask tough questions, including saying , “Quiet, piggy” to a Bloomberg reporter, calling another CNN journalist “corrupt”, and storming out of NBC’s Meet the Press after calling the moderator “crooked or stupid”. Other journalists condemned the White House’s personal attack against Holmes, with one of her colleagues at CNN saying : “Kristen is an incredible reporter, person and, above all, mother. I don’t understand such a reaction to a journalist asking the president for his response to something a Democratic senator has leveled against him.” Explore more on these topics Donald Trump news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed US news US politics Midterms 2026 World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness

Photograph: Mike Bowers/The Guardian One Nation One Nation’s Malcolm Roberts ‘in two minds’ about whether gay people should be equal Footage shows senator on stage at the Church and State conference responding to question about party’s director James Ashby Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Tory Shepherd Tue 25 Aug 2026 11.00 EDT Last modified on Tue 25 Aug 2026 11.01 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google One Nation’s Malcolm Roberts told a conference earlier this year that he was in “two minds” about whether gay people should have equal rights. In footage from June’s Church and State conference, released on Sunday, the senator can be seen responding to a question about James Ashby, the party’s director, who is gay. Both Roberts and the One Nation leader, Pauline Hanson , appeared at the conservative Christian conference. In the footage, Roberts described Ashby as bright, honest and straight. “Well, straight in one way,” he joked. An audience member then asked Roberts what Christians should think about Ashby. Roberts responded by referring to the late American bishop and gay rights advocate John Shelby Spong, citing him as saying that after women and black people were no longer recognised as “inferior”, gay people were next. “Now I’m in two minds about that,” Roberts said. “So I haven’t got a firm position on it myself other than I don’t, I’m not homosexual and I can’t, I can’t understand it. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email “But there have been a number of homosexuals who are very, very prominent in many, many fields throughout history. So all I know is that in this environment, James is not morally sound. But from what I’ve seen of him, his honesty, his integrity, his ability, he is sound. “So if you pardon me, I haven’t made up my mind, but there are a number of people in society in very prominent positions in the arts, sports, science, business, politics, who are homosexual. “And I don’t think we can afford to ban them. So it’s difficult.” The chief executive of Equality Australia, Anna Brown, said it was “genuinely shocking” that a One Nation senator would talk about “banning” people. One Nation’s immigration policy is hard to define – even by its own MPs Read more “As though something so incompatible with a democratic society could be an acceptable option,” she said. “The idea that One Nation or its senators think that this could be an idea that’s on the table, or even a matter of legitimate debate, is incredibly chilling. “And perhaps it’s worth reminding the senator that being gay and a person of deep faith are not mutually exclusive, and neither makes someone any more or less morally sound.” The organiser of the conference, Dave Pellowe, said in the same forum that “loud, screaming activists” had held American medical health professions to ransom “until they capitulated to delisting same-sex attraction as something that needed treatment, as an illness”. Roberts is also seen in the footage vowing to push for the party to adopt a blanket abortion ban, contradicting Hanson’s position . skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion 6:27 Barnaby Joyce suggests One Nation could welcome some refugees while barring other migrants – video He also said he would push for the party to claim that life begins at conception. In an Instagram post from earlier this year, also from the conference, Hanson can be seen saying she “ had to have a conversation ” with the Farrer MP, David Farley, after he commented that the current immigration intake of 306,000 was “probably not” too much. As leader she sometimes had to “call the shots”, she said in the latest footage. Since Farley’s migration comments, there have been multiple contradictions and changes in the anti-immigration party’s policy. Church and State describes itself as a “Christian political education ministry” teaching people to look at political issues and candidates through the lens of Scripture. One Nation representatives have made frequent comments about homosexuality on other occasions. Earlier this month, the MP Barnaby Joyce described One Nation as “ one of the gayest parties in Australia ” after its failed candidate Parminder Singh described homosexuality as a mental illness. Hanson then said she didn’t like the Mardi Gras and that “your own personal sexuality should be kept behind closed doors”. Ashby has said as a “ gay bloke ” he doesn’t like the rainbow flag. Jason Virgo, who is gay, was elected as a One Nation MP in the South Australian election in March, while his newly elected colleague in the upper house, Cory Bernardi, said he stood by his 2012 comments linking same-sex marriage to polygamy and bestiality. In the Church and State footage, Roberts also discussed various conspiracy theories and said family law changes made since 1975 – including the introduction of no-fault divorce – were “tearing apart this country”. “It’s deliberate because they’re after the family. They’re after anything that can stand up to communism,” he said. Malcolm Roberts, James Ashby and One Nation did not respond to a request for comment. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cwm2.text: Image source, Europa Press via Getty Images Image caption, Protests have taken place in Madrid, Barcelona, Seville, Malaga and Cadiz in response to the housing crisis By Alys Davies Â and Â Guy Hedgecoe ,Â Reporting from Madrid Published 29 September 2026, 13:14 BST Updated 1 hour ago Spain's coalition government has approved new housing measures following protests over the country's housing crisis, sparked by the eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her home in Madrid last week. Ministers met on Tuesday to discuss the proposals, which include a ban on evictions until 2030. Announcing the measures, Health Minister MÃ³nica GarcÃ­a said they would bring relief to more than five million people - but opposition politician MÃ­riam Nogueras said the agreement left "small landlords out in the cold". The proposals - which have been presented in the form of two decrees - come into effect immediately, but must be approved by Congress within a month, although the government hopes to hold the vote as soon as this Friday. Pedro SÃ¡nchez's leftist coalition government lacks a majority in parliament and has struggled to get right-leaning parties to approve previous decrees. In April, a decree seeking to roll over rental contracts was blocked by right-leaning parties. GarcÃ­a, of the Sumar alliance, said other measures agreed upon on Tuesday included the rolling over of contracts until 2028; stricter regulation of short-term and room rentals; and banning the purchase of housing by investment firms. "It is time to intervene in the speculative housing market and start striking a balance between ordinary citizens and vulture funds," GarcÃ­a said. Referencing the protests, she added: "Thanks to the mobilisations and the encampments. Without you, this would not have been possible." But Nogueras, spokeswoman for the centre-right Catalan nationalists of Junts party, said: "We all agreed that evictions - where the property is owned by a fund, a vulture fund, run by someone managing millions of euros - obviously need to be stopped. "Lumping together in this category those who have invested their savings in a flat, a restaurant or a property - putting them all in the same basket - is a mistake," she told Spanish public broadcaster RTVE. The minority government, which is made up of the SÃ¡nchez's ruling Socialists and junior partner the Sumar alliance, has 30 days from the decrees' publication to reach an agreement in parliament. Housing Minister Isabel RodrÃ­guez urged political parties to support the decrees after the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal last week. "Congress has the opportunity to tell Maricarmen that her suffering was worth it... and that many people will benefit from her battle", she said. But Valeria Racu, a spokeswoman for the Madrid Tenants' Union, said the battle had "only just begun", and called for more protests across Spain next weekend. "We all have our eyes on the text, on the small print, to make sure this is the Maricarmen decree," added Alicia del RÃ­o, another spokeswoman for the organisation. Image source, Lima/Getty Images Image caption, Maricarmen Abascal was evicted from her apartment in Madrid on a stretcher on Wednesday The two decrees approved by the cabinet contain enough to at least suggest that the government has been listening carefully to the demands of the activists who have been protesting in Madrid, Barcelona and elsewhere in recent days. The temporary ban on evictions, the rolling over of rental contracts and the ban on investment firms - or "vulture funds" as the government has termed them - buying property are all the kinds of policies that have been discussed by housing activists in recent days. Pablo Bustinduy, minister of social rights, described the measures approved by the cabinet as "a first step towards the economic and social transformation of the country". Bustinduy and his Sumar alliance had entered the negotiations with SÃ¡nchez's Socialists determined to take a stand on this issue, which is one they feel strongly about. Sumar's tough stance was a major reason why talks between the coalition partners on the decrees went down to the wire ahead of Tuesday's cabinet meeting. While the relatively bold new measures may please many on the left, they have raised the hackles of the Junts, whose support is again likely to be needed to approve them. Junts and other parties on the right tend to be reluctant to intervene in the housing market, particularly if it means tipping the balance of the law in favour of tenants and against landlords, many of who are their natural electorate. The question now is whether the social momentum generated by the Maricarmen Abascal case will override such reservations and manage to ensure this package of measures becomes law. Abascal, who was admitted to hospital after being forcibly removed from the apartment on a stretcher, was unable to attend the meeting and is yet to sign the deal. Abascal's father first rented the flat in 1956 and she had continued to live in it after her parents died, with a cap on the rent, until investment company UrbagestiÃ³n bought the property in 2018. It raised the monthly rent to more than her monthly pension, leaving her unable to pay it. Abascal's case is not unique. In the north-eastern city of Zaragoza, another woman's eviction was temporarily suspended on Tuesday, the European Pressphoto Agency reported. Esmeralda Tejero, 51, has lived in a flat in the city for eight years with her 11-year-old daughter, but stopped paying her rent some time ago as she could not afford it on top of her daily living costs, she told Catalan newspaper el PeriÃ³dico on Monday. Protests calling for housing relief measures broke out last week in Madrid and have spread to other cities including Barcelona, Seville, Malaga and Cadiz. Thousands marched through the capital on Saturday demanding stronger protection for tenants in the face of a housing shortage and soaring rents. Hundreds of tents have been set up in the famous public square of Puerta del Sol since. Image source, Europa Press via Getty Images Image caption, Protesters remained at the tent encampment in Puerta del Sol on Tuesday The Bank of Spain estimates the country is short of 700,000 homes, based on the gap between demand and new construction. House prices have risen by 12.2% in the past year, according to figures for the second quarter of 2026 from national statistics institute INE. The shortage in rental housing means that costs rose by 8.5% in 2025, according to real estate firm Idealista, with Madrid alone seeing an increase of 9.7% in rents. It said Barcelona and Madrid were Spain's most expensive cities to rent a home, at â¬23.80 per square metre and â¬22.70 per square metre respectively.
